name: Straight sleeve
source: Based on Winifred Aldrich, Metric Pattern Cutting for Women's Wear, 6th ed. (Wiley-Blackwell, 2015), the one-piece sleeve block. Deviations: the sleeve cap is constructed rather than drawn: each half runs from the crown to its underarm point as a convex circular arc, a vertical straight piece where the cap is higher than the half is wide, and a concave circular arc of the same turn; the cap height is not measured but solved (a few Newton steps written as formulas) so that the cap equals the armhole imported from the bodice plus cap_ease, and the crown is shifted so that each half matches its own armhole half (back and front armholes differ); all cap ease lies between the notches, which sit at the same arc distance from the underarm points as the bodice notches from the side points, with a crown notch matching the shoulder seam; the underarm seams taper straight to a hem of wrist plus ease_wrist, centred under the bicep line; the ease and the constants (ease_upper_arm, ease_wrist, cap_ease, cap_convex_share) are our own starting values, set and pinned by the engine tests, to be adjusted after test fitting (a toile/provsömnad).

formulas.cap_lf_1: (cap_wf_1 * cap_wf_1 + cap_af_1 * cap_af_1) * rad(atan2(cap_af_1, cap_wf_1)) / cap_af_1 + max(0, cap_h_0 - cap_wf_1)
